paragraphs: Overall credibility is unknown, so the results below should not be read as converged or trustworthy. For static step s1, the reaction balance check passed, and the maximum-stress and maximum-displacement convergence checks passed. The mesh quality check is unknown: second-order elements on curved surfaces became too distorted after promotion, so straight-edged second-order elements were used and the curved surfaces are approximated by chords. Stress near curved surfaces may therefore deviate noticeably.

Static results for s1: the maximum von Mises stress (excluding constrained faces) is {{s1.vm_max_mpa}}, the maximum displacement is {{s1.u_max_mm}}, and the material yield strength is {{s1.strength_mpa}}. The maximum stress over the three mesh levels is {{s1.conv2.level0}}, {{s1.conv2.level1}} and {{s1.conv2.level2}}. The maximum displacement over the three levels is {{s1.conv3.level0}}, {{s1.conv3.level1}} and {{s1.conv3.level2}}. The safety factor is not given, because the credibility checks did not pass (overall status unknown).

For modal step m1, the first four natural frequencies are {{m1.f1_hz}}, {{m1.f2_hz}}, {{m1.f3_hz}} and {{m1.f4_hz}}. They correspond to rotational speeds of {{m1.f1_rpm}}, {{m1.f2_rpm}}, {{m1.f3_rpm}} and {{m1.f4_rpm}}. The first two modes are very close in frequency.

Limitations: the model is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions and were excluded from the maximum-stress evaluation. Stress at sharp corners grows with mesh refinement (a theoretical singularity) and should not be used directly as a design basis. Only the part's own mass and stiffness are included, so attached masses are ignored. Supports are ideal, and real bearing stiffness would lower the frequencies.
suggestions: Reduce the element size on the curved surfaces so that there are several element layers across them, then rerun to clear the mesh quality check.
Re-check mesh quality after refinement and confirm that second-order elements with curved edges can be used on the curved surfaces.
Have an engineer review the sharp corners manually and add a fillet or use a local stress method instead of relying on the corner peak stress.
Add the mass of attached components to the modal model if they are present in service.
Replace the ideal supports with measured or estimated bearing stiffness to obtain realistic natural frequencies.
Compare the natural frequencies against the actual operating speed range, with particular attention to the closely spaced first two modes.
